name: Sumerian
summary_description: The earliest known civilization in southern Mesopotamia, credited with inventing writing, the wheel, and urban society

name: Akkadian
summary_description: First empire in Mesopotamia, uniting Sumerian and Akkadian-speaking peoples under Sargon of Akkad

name: Babylonian
summary_description: Major Mesopotamian civilization known for Hammurabi's code, astronomy, and mathematics

name: Assyrian
summary_description: Powerful militaristic civilization known for its vast empire, library of Ashurbanipal, and monumental architecture

name: Ancient Egyptian
summary_description: One of the longest-lasting civilizations, known for pyramids, hieroglyphs, and pharaonic culture

name: Classical Greek
summary_description: Collection of city-states that developed democracy, philosophy, and classical arts

name: Roman
summary_description: Vast empire spanning Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East, known for law, engineering, and governance

name: Persian
summary_description: The Achaemenid Empire, the largest empire of the ancient world, known for tolerance and road systems

name: Mauryan
summary_description: First pan-Indian empire under Chandragupta and Ashoka, spreading Buddhism and establishing governance

name: Gupta
summary_description: Golden age of India marked by advances in science, mathematics, art, and literature

name: Han Chinese
summary_description: One of China's golden ages, establishing Confucianism as state ideology and opening the Silk Road

name: Tang Chinese
summary_description: Cosmopolitan golden age of Chinese culture, poetry, and technological innovation
sources: ["Old Book of Tang","New Book of Tang"]

name: Song Chinese
summary_description: Era of economic revolution, technological innovation including printing, gunpowder, and the compass

name: Ming Chinese
summary_description: Period of cultural refinement, construction of the Great Wall, and Zheng He's maritime expeditions

name: Mongol
summary_description: Largest contiguous land empire in history, connecting East and West through trade and conquest

name: Ottoman
summary_description: Long-lasting empire bridging Europe, Asia, and Africa, known for religious tolerance and architectural splendor

name: Byzantine
summary_description: Continuation of the Roman Empire in the east, preserving classical knowledge and developing Orthodox Christianity

name: Aztec
summary_description: Dominant Mesoamerican civilization known for monumental architecture, complex calendar, and sacrificial rituals

name: Inca
summary_description: Largest empire in pre-Columbian America, known for road systems, terraced agriculture, and quipu record-keeping

name: Maya
summary_description: Advanced civilization known for hieroglyphic writing, astronomy, mathematics, and monumental pyramids

name: Khmer
summary_description: Powerful empire centered on Angkor, known for massive temple complexes and sophisticated water management

name: Mali
summary_description: Wealthy West African empire known for trade in gold and salt, and the legendary pilgrimage of Mansa Musa

name: Songhai
summary_description: Successor to Mali, one of the largest African empires, centered on trade and Islamic scholarship

name: Great Zimbabwe
summary_description: Powerful trading state known for its monumental stone architecture without mortar

name: Carthaginian
summary_description: Major Mediterranean trading power and rival to Rome, known for maritime prowess and Hannibal

name: Phoenician
summary_description: Maritime traders who developed the alphabet and established colonies across the Mediterranean

name: Indus Valley
summary_description: Bronze Age civilization with advanced urban planning, standardized weights, and undeciphered script

name: Shang
summary_description: First historically verified Chinese dynasty, known for oracle bones, bronze vessels, and ancestor worship

name: Hittite
summary_description: Major Bronze Age power that rivaled Egypt, known for iron smelting and diplomatic treaties

name: Viking
summary_description: Seafaring warriors, traders, and explorers who spread across Europe and the North Atlantic

name: Celtic
summary_description: Iron Age culture known for distinctive art, druidic religion, and warrior aristocracy

name: Mughal
summary_description: Indo-Islamic empire known for architectural masterpieces like the Taj Mahal and cultural syncretism

name: Sasanian
summary_description: Last pre-Islamic Persian empire, a major world power rivaling Rome/Byzantium

name: Umayyad
summary_description: First hereditary Islamic dynasty, spreading Islam from Spain to Central Asia

name: Abbasid
summary_description: Islamic golden age of science, philosophy, and culture centered on Baghdad

name: Zhou
summary_description: Longest Chinese dynasty, giving rise to Confucianism, Taoism, and the Hundred Schools of Thought

name: Qin
summary_description: First unified Chinese empire, known for the Great Wall, terracotta army, and standardization

name: Qing
summary_description: Last Chinese imperial dynasty, expanding China to its greatest territorial extent

name: Srivijayan
summary_description: Maritime empire controlling the Strait of Malacca, a major center of Buddhist learning

name: Minoan
summary_description: Bronze Age civilization on Crete known for palatial complexes, bull-leaping, and maritime trade

name: Mycenaean
summary_description: Bronze Age warrior civilization of mainland Greece, inspiration for Homeric epics

name: Etruscan
summary_description: Pre-Roman Italian civilization known for sophisticated art, engineering, and religious practices

name: Nubian
summary_description: African civilization along the upper Nile, rivals and successors to Egyptian pharaohs

name: Axumite
summary_description: Major trading empire in the Horn of Africa, one of the first states to adopt Christianity

name: Benin Kingdom
summary_description: Powerful West African kingdom renowned for its bronze sculptures and sophisticated court culture

name: Swahili Coast
summary_description: Network of trading city-states along the East African coast, blending African, Arab, and Indian Ocean cultures

name: Tibetan
summary_description: Himalayan civilization centered on Vajrayana Buddhism and a unique monastic culture

name: Polynesian
summary_description: Master navigators who settled the vast Pacific triangle, developing unique island cultures

name: Aboriginal Australian
summary_description: World's oldest continuous culture with sophisticated knowledge systems, art traditions, and land management

name: Jomon
summary_description: Prehistoric Japanese culture known for distinctive cord-marked pottery and sedentary hunter-gathering

name: Mississippian
summary_description: Complex chiefdom culture of eastern North America known for massive earthen mounds and Cahokia

name: Ancestral Puebloan
summary_description: Southwestern culture known for cliff dwellings, pottery, and sophisticated irrigation systems

name: Olmec
summary_description: Mother culture of Mesoamerica, known for colossal stone heads, jade work, and early writing

name: Teotihuacan
summary_description: Massive pre-Columbian city and influential culture with the Pyramid of the Sun

name: Toltec
summary_description: Warrior civilization that bridged Classic and Postclassic Mesoamerica

name: Zapotec
summary_description: One of the earliest Mesoamerican writing systems and major urban center at Monte Alban

name: Chavin
summary_description: Early Andean civilization known for jaguar imagery and the influential Chavin art style

name: Moche
summary_description: Pre-Inca Peruvian culture known for elaborate ceramics, metalwork, and the Lords of Sipan

name: Tiwanaku

name: Chimu
summary_description: Pre-Inca coastal kingdom with the largest adobe city in the Americas

name: Gaulish
summary_description: Celtic peoples of France known for sophisticated agriculture, metalwork, and hill forts

name: Scythian
summary_description: Nomadic warrior culture of the Eurasian steppe known for gold artwork and mounted archery

name: Xiongnu

name: Kushan
summary_description: Empire connecting China, India, and Rome, fostering Gandharan Buddhist art

name: Parthian
summary_description: Iranian empire that succeeded the Seleucids and rivaled Rome for centuries

name: Seleucid
summary_description: Hellenistic empire spanning from Anatolia to Central Asia, blending Greek and Eastern cultures

name: Ptolemaic Egyptian
summary_description: Greek-ruled Egyptian kingdom blending Egyptian and Hellenistic culture, home to the Library of Alexandria

name: Nabataean
summary_description: Arabian trading kingdom that carved the city of Petra from rock, controlling incense trade routes

name: Palmyrene
summary_description: Oasis trading city at the crossroads of Roman and Parthian empires

name: Georgian
summary_description: Ancient Caucasian civilization with one of the world's unique alphabets and rich wine culture

name: Armenian
summary_description: Ancient civilization, first nation to adopt Christianity, with distinctive alphabet and architecture

name: Heian Japanese
summary_description: Golden age of Japanese court culture, producing the Tale of Genji and refined aesthetic traditions

name: Joseon Korean

name: Goryeo Korean
summary_description: Korean dynasty known for celadon ceramics, metal movable type, and Buddhist cultural achievements

summary_description: Peak of Khmer civilization centered on the city of Angkor, the world's largest preindustrial city

name: Champa
summary_description: Hindu-influenced maritime kingdom of central Vietnam known for tower temples

name: Pagan
summary_description: First unified Burmese kingdom, known for thousands of Buddhist temples on the plains of Bagan

name: Majapahit
summary_description: Last major Hindu-Buddhist empire of Indonesia, controlling much of maritime Southeast Asia

name: Medieval European
summary_description: Post-Roman European civilization centered on feudalism, Christianity, and Gothic architecture

name: Islamic Golden Age
summary_description: Period of extraordinary scientific, cultural, and economic flourishing in the Islamic world

name: Venetian
summary_description: Maritime republic and trading power, known for glass, art, and the unique canal city

name: Kievan Rus
summary_description: Medieval federation of Slavic tribes that became the foundation of Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus

name: Ghana Empire

name: Kanem-Bornu
summary_description: Long-lasting African empire centered on Lake Chad, important in trans-Saharan trade

name: Mapuche
summary_description: Indigenous people of south-central Chile and Argentina who resisted Inca and Spanish conquest

name: Maori

name: Hawaiian

name: Iroquois

name: Khwarezmian
summary_description: Powerful Persianate empire of Central Asia destroyed by the Mongol invasion

name: Timurid
summary_description: Empire of Timur known for architectural splendor and the Timurid Renaissance

name: Nok

name: Natufian

name: Catalhoyuk

name: Yamnaya
summary_description: Proto-Indo-European steppe pastoralists whose migrations transformed Eurasia

name: Linear Pottery
summary_description: First farming culture of central Europe, spreading agriculture from the Near East

name: Bell Beaker
summary_description: Widespread European culture known for distinctive bell-shaped pottery and metalworking

summary_description: Bronze Age culture of Thailand known for painted pottery and early metalworking

summary_description: Oldest known civilization in the Americas, with monumental architecture but no pottery or writing

name: Gobekli Tepe
summary_description: Builders of the world's oldest known monumental architecture, predating agriculture
